profile_text.body:
Microsoft is a public company founded in 1975 and headquartered in Redmond, WA. The harvested content comes from the Power Automate product page, which describes Power Automate as a tool for automating workflows and business processes across apps, systems, and websites using AI-powered, digital, and robotic process automation. The page includes customer quotes describing headcount reductions in data validation work attributed to generative AI and Power Automate, and references a Gartner Magic Quadrant for Robotic Process Automation report dated June 23, 2025, credited to analysts Arthur Villa, Saikat Ray, Melanie Alexander, and Sachin Joshi.

Microsoft's tracked AI products span several categories, including Microsoft Power Automate AI for enterprise workflow automation with Copilot and data loss prevention integration, Microsoft Copilot embedded across Microsoft 365, Azure OpenAI Service for accessing OpenAI models within Azure with enterprise content filtering and Entra ID integration, Azure Machine Learning as an MLOps platform with AutoML and a model registry, AutoGen as a multi-agent conversation framework developed through Microsoft Research, Microsoft Designer for image and design generation, Microsoft Teams AI for meeting recaps and Copilot integration, SharePoint AI for enterprise content management, and Microsoft Clipchamp AI for video editing with auto-caption and text-to-speech features. The company reported revenue of $331,839,000,000 for the period ending June 30, 2026, filed as a 10-K, and trades publicly under the ticker MSFT with CIK 0000789019.

On the litigation side, Microsoft is a named defendant in The New York Times Co. v. Microsoft Corp. and OpenAI, filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, and is associated with the related matter Authors Guild v. OpenAI, Inc. in the same court, both of which concern AI-related copyright claims.
